record.one_liner: Amazon Selling Partner API: programmatic access to seller and vendor data and operations on Amazon marketplaces.
record.auth_notes: Public apps use OAuth 2.0 via Login with Amazon (LWA) with a refresh token renewed annually. Private apps are self-authorized from the Solution Provider Portal console, which also generates an LWA refresh token (max 10 authorizations per app). No api_key or basic method was found in the fetched pages.
record.access_notes: Developer access requires a Professional selling account, which costs $39.99/month plus selling fees. Individual accounts are not eligible. Developer Central access and SP-API integration are limited to Professional accounts.
record.api_notes: Operations are gated by roles (for example Product Listing, Pricing). Breadth was not verified against the full operation catalog; rated moderate as a guess. REST style is inferred from the HTTP host and x-amz header model in the connection docs and was not stated explicitly in the pages opened.
record.blocker_notes: The API requires a Professional selling account at $39.99/month plus selling fees before any developer credentials can be created. Once that plan is in place, private-app self-authorization needs no vendor approval. The official MCP (local npm package from the Amazon org) runs against your own SP-API credentials.

evidence.quote: Public applications must use OAuth 2.0 to obtain authorization from selling partners to call the SP-API on the selling partner's behalf.
The self-authorization process generates an LWA refresh token.
Yes, only Professional selling accounts can access Developer Central and integrate with SP-API.
A Professional selling account is $39.99/month + selling fees.
Only Professional Selling Accounts can register to develop or integrate with Selling Partner API. Individual accounts are not eligible.
An LWA access token must be included in calls to all operations except restricted operations, which return Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Local MCP for SP-API brings this to the SP-API ecosystem as a consolidated npm package bundling MCP servers for Amazon Selling Partner API development.
You must have a Professional selling account and be the primary account user to create an SP-API developer profile.
